title: The Disappearing Index Effect
one_line: The S&P 500 inclusion effect fell from +7.4% abnormal return in the 1990s to ~0.3% in the 2010s (deletions similar), as liquidity provision improved and most additions became mid-cap migrations.

findings.statement: Similar declines in Russell and Nasdaq-100.

why.pattern: Market adaptation to predictable index demand.

reported_results.headline: The S&P 500 inclusion effect fell from +7.4% abnormal return in the 1990s to ~0.3% in the 2010s (deletions similar), as liquidity provision improved and most additions became mid-cap migrations.

tradable_edge: Stock-level; another example of a published flow effect decaying.
data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 3), not by the weekly pipeline.
